equation_request.abstract: In recent years, deep learning has had a profound impact on machine learning and artificial intelligence. At the same time, algorithms for quantum computers have been shown to efficiently solve some problems that are intractable on conventional, classical computers. We show that quantum computing not only reduces the time required to train a deep restricted Boltzmann machine, but also provides a richer and more comprehensive framework for deep learning than classical computing and leads to significant improvements in the optimization of the underlying objective function. Our quantum methods also permit efficient training of full Boltzmann machines and multi–layer, fully connected models and do not have well known classical counterparts.

specification.problem: Prepare the Gibbs distribution P(v,h)=exp(-E(v,h))/Z of a small Boltzmann machine by mean-field-product-state preparation plus an ancilla rotation with postselection, and read out <v_i h_j> to form the gradient dO/dw_ij = <v_i h_j>_data - <v_i h_j>_model (Wiebe-Kapoor-Svore style).
specification.reconstruction_scope: One tiny instance: 1 visible and 1 hidden unit (or 2+1), a single weight w, biases b_v,b_h, a single ancilla, postselected exactly on the statevector, then <v h>_model from ZZ parity, and <v h>_data by clamping v. Excluded: QRAM data oracle, full amplitude-estimation phase-estimation register, the paper's exact error analysis, deep multi-layer models beyond a small fully connected example, and any speedup verification.

symbols.meaning: binary unit value of visible/hidden unit i, x_i in {0,1}; qubit state |x_i>
mean-field product distribution with Q(x)=prod_i q_i^{x_i}(1-q_i)^{1-x_i}
constant with exp(-E(x)) <= kappa Q(x) for all x

equations.label: Energy
equations.latex: E(x)=-\sum_i b_i x_i-\sum_{i<j} w_{ij} x_i x_j
equations.description: Boltzmann machine energy over all visible and hidden units (full connectivity allowed); the sketch writes it with the sum over all pairs.
equations.justification: Standard definition; the abstract names Boltzmann machines but gives no formula.
assumptions: No separate constant offset; the pair sum counts each pair once

equations.label: Gibbs and mean-field distributions
equations.description: Replace with Q(x)=prod_i q_i^{x_i}(1-q_i)^{1-x_i}, q_i=sin^2(theta_i/2), prepared by Ry(theta_i)|0> on each qubit.
equations.justification: Standard mean-field and Gibbs definitions. Ry(theta)|0>=cos(theta/2)|0>+sin(theta/2)|1> gives P(1)=sin^2(theta/2). Note the Q formula in this latex is a typographical simplification; use the product of q_i factors.
assumptions: q_i are mean-field marginals computed classically and strictly inside (0,1)

equations.label: Ancilla rotation and postselection
equations.description: Ancilla Ry angle 2 arcsin(sqrt(e^{-E}/(kappa Q))) controlled on x, computed from classical values for tiny instances. Post-selecting ancilla=1 yields sum_x sqrt(P(x))|x>. Because Q is normalized, P_succ=Z/kappa; this equals Z/(kappa Z_Q) in the sketch's convention if Q is unnormalized.
equations.justification: Sketch construction; the abstract does not give the rotation. Implementable for small n as a multiplexed Ry (uniformly controlled rotation) using standard gates, since the rotation angle is a function of x computed classically; the energy-into-phase route is an alternative that needs an energy register.
assumptions: Angle table is built from known b,w (the model parameters are known to the builder, not a hidden black box)

equations.label: Model expectation
equations.latex: \langle v_i h_j\rangle_{model}=\sum_x P(x)x_i x_j=\frac{1-\langle Z_i\rangle-\langle Z_j\rangle+\langle Z_iZ_j\rangle}{4}
equations.description: Model correlator read from postselected Gibbs state via Z expectations (Z|x>=(-1)^x|x>).

equations.label: Data expectation with clamped visible units
equations.description: Visible qubits set to training vector x^(k) by X gates, hidden units Gibbs-prepared conditioned on v (same construction with v fixed, energy restricted to h), averaged over data classically (looped) in the small case.
equations.abstract_quote: leads to significant improvements in the optimization of the underlying objective function
equations.justification: Training gradient requires data and model terms; the exact data-term circuit is inferred from the sketch, not stated in the abstract.
assumptions: Small training set looped over classically; no QRAM

equations.label: Gradient and update
equations.latex: \frac{\partial O}{\partial w_{ij}}=\langle v_i h_j\rangle_{data}-\langle v_i h_j\rangle_{model},\quad w_{ij}\leftarrow w_{ij}+\eta\,\frac{\partial O}{\partial w_{ij}}
equations.description: Log-likelihood gradient and classical gradient ascent update with learning rate eta.

registers.name: vis
registers.role: visible units, qubit index i is bit i (little-endian)

registers.name: ae
registers.role: amplitude estimation register; omitted in the exact-statevector scope

specification.initial_state: All qubits |0>; apply Ry(theta_i) on each vis/hid qubit to make the mean-field state sum_x sqrt(Q(x))|x>.

steps.description: Classically compute mean-field marginals q_i and theta_i=2 arcsin(sqrt(q_i)); choose kappa >= max_x e^{-E}/Q.
Prepare the mean-field product state with Ry rotations.
Apply the x-controlled ancilla rotation (multiplexed Ry from the classical angle table) so ancilla=1 has amplitude sqrt(e^{-E}/(kappa Q)).
Postselect ancilla=1 (exact projection on the statevector, or conditioned counts; optionally Grover amplification of the ancilla-1 subspace) to get the Gibbs state.
Read the model correlator via Z and ZZ expectations; repeat with v clamped to each training vector for the data term.

specification.measurement: Measure vis and hid qubits and the ancilla in the Z basis; keep shots with ancilla=1. Qiskit little-endian: bit i of the counts key (read from the right) is qubit i.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Estimate <x_i x_j> from postselected counts or from the identity in eq_4; average data terms; compute gradient and update weights.
assumptions: Smallest construction: 1-2 visible and 1 hidden unit with a known tiny weight set
Rotation angles are computed classically from known parameters, which is legitimate here as the machine parameters are not a hidden oracle
Amplitude estimation replaced by direct readout; the O(sqrt(kappa)/epsilon) scaling is not tested
missing_information: The abstract gives no equations; all constructions come from the sketch and background
Exact energy-oracle or phase-based implementation of the paper
Exact amplitude estimation and Grover circuit details and error bounds
Handling of the biased gradient for general deep models
